MongoDB Series · Lecture 06 · After $unwind, items is one object, so "$items.price" works

Amount = price × quantity

Step 5 · $sort + $limit
Top 3 products by revenue
{ $unwind: "$items" }, { $group: { _id: "$items.product",   revenue: { $sum: { $multiply: ["$items.price", "$items.quantity"] } } } }, { $sort: { revenue: -1 } }, { $limit: 3 }
Without $match
1. Laptop · ₹1,22,000 2. Mobile · ₹53,000 3. Tablet · ₹18,000 ← cancelled!
With $match: Delivered first
1. Laptop · ₹1,22,000 2. Mobile · ₹53,000 3. Watch · ₹5,000
MongoDB Series · Lecture 06 · A "bestseller" that was never paid for is a bug, not a bestseller
$bucket · use case: small, medium, big sales
Drop numbers into ranges
db.sales.aggregate([ { $bucket: {   groupBy: "$amount",   boundaries: [0, 100, 300, Infinity],   default: "Other",   output: { count: { $sum: 1 },           totalAmount: { $sum: "$amount" } } } } ])

MongoDB Series · Lecture 06 · Each range includes its lower boundary, excludes the upper · _id = the lower boundary
$bucket on line items · an interview favourite
Shop by price range
{ $unwind: "$items" }, { $bucket: { groupBy: "$items.price", boundaries: [0, 2000, 10000, 30000, 70000],   default: "Premium",   output: { count: { $sum: 1 }, products: { $push: "$items.product" } } } }

MongoDB Series · Lecture 06 · Like SQL LEFT JOIN: an order with no matching customer gets an empty array
$lookup + $unwind + $project
Orders with customer names
{ $lookup: { from: "customers", localField: "customerId",             foreignField: "customerId", as: "customer" } }, { $unwind: "$customer" },  // array of 1 → plain object { $project: { _id: 0, orderId: 1, name: "$customer.name", city: 1, status: 1 } }

MongoDB Series · Lecture 06 · $unwind is the one stage that can make MORE documents
Mini project · loyalty rewards
Our top 3 customers, by name
db.orders.aggregate([   { $match: { status: "Delivered" } },   { $unwind: "$items" },   { $group: { _id: "$customerId", spent: { $sum:     { $multiply: ["$items.price", "$items.quantity"] } } } },   { $sort: { spent: -1 } }, { $limit: 3 },   { $lookup: { from: "customers", localField: "_id",     foreignField: "customerId", as: "c" } },   { $unwind: "$c" },   { $project: { _id: 0, name: "$c.name", spent: 1 } } ])
1. Neha
₹87,000
2. Amit
₹64,100
3. Rahul
₹31,500
MongoDB Series · Lecture 06 · Join AFTER $limit: 3 lookups instead of 10 — less work, less I/O
Cheat sheet
Today's new tools
$unwind: "$items"
one document per array element
$multiply: [a, b]
calculate inside $project or $sum
$bucket
groupBy + boundaries + default + output
$lookup
from · localField · foreignField · as
$match first
answer the right business question
$lookup late
after $limit, join only what you keep
